lecture_title: SU(5) Multiplets, Leptoquark Gauge Bosons, and Proton Decay

assets.name: lecture_10_figure_02.png
assets.rationale: The completed board is unobstructed and shows the symmetric triplet, antisymmetric singlet, and their relation in one view.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The other way is unique; there is only one antisymmetric combination.

assets.name: lecture_10_figure_04.png
assets.rationale: The lecturer has moved clear of the board and the mixed product, N squared minus one, and adjoint label are simultaneously visible.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The adjoint representation has dimension N squared minus one.
assets.caption_hint: N times N-bar and the adjoint

assets.name: lecture_10_figure_05.png
assets.rationale: This later view is unobstructed and preserves the completed antisymmetric matter matrix, block partition, and checked color labels.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: That is the pattern of SU(5).

assets.name: lecture_10_figure_06.png
assets.rationale: The full heavy-boson exchange, spectator up quark, positron, and proton bracket are visible without body occlusion.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: What kind of particles can you make out of a quark and an antiquark?

assets.name: lecture_10_figure_07.png
assets.rationale: The inverse-coupling trajectories, circled near-meeting, and 10 to the 16 GeV scale are visible together after the drawing is complete.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The unification scale really should be 10 to the 16 GeV.
assets.caption_hint: inverse couplings near the unification scale
